body: I think this is related to https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3308. In particular, MRO is not recalculated in third pass for synthetic types like named tuples. I think the solution should be similar to https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/3322 - add corresponding recalculation in the third pass. After #3322 is merged this should be quite easy.

I can reproduce the second traceback when annotating with a NamedTuple type before that type's definition: 

```python
from typing import NamedTuple

def get_state(proc: 'Process') -> int:
    return proc.state

class Process(NamedTuple):
     state: int
```
This kind of annotation came up for me when writing a decorator to be used on the methods of the new NamedTuple.

mypy version: `0.520-dev-7670ac9a6527708faf226039d600da6e7e596462`

Line 52 is `dsn=cfg.dsn,`

SentryConfig is a typing.NamedTuple class.
obs.config imports `no_sentry`, which is why I use the `if TYPE_CHECKING` and forward reference

<details><summary>File triggering error</summary>

```
"""
Utilities for interacting with Sentry (sentry.io)
"""
from typing import TypeVar, Dict, Any, Optional, TYPE_CHECKING

import raven  # type: ignore
from raven.processors import Processor  # type: ignore
from raven.utils import varmap  # type: ignore

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    # Avoid circular import
    from .config import SentryConfig

A = TypeVar('A')

# Sentinel value
_no_sentry = object()


def no_sentry(obj: A) -> A:
    """
    Decorates an object that should not be included in sentry's stack trace locals
    """
    obj._no_sentry = _no_sentry  # type: ignore
    return obj


class GenericLocalProcessor(Processor):  # type: ignore
    """
    Can be subclassed by overriding `should_remove`, which will get each local name and value in traces
    """

    def should_remove(self, name: str, value: object) -> bool:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def filter_stacktrace(self, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        for frame in data.get('frames', []):
            if 'vars' not in frame:
                continue
            frame['vars'] = varmap(lambda name, var: "REDACTED" if self.should_remove(name, var) else var,
                                   frame['vars'])


class RemoveNoSentryProcessor(GenericLocalProcessor):
    def should_remove(self, name: str, value: object) -> bool:
        return hasattr(value, '_no_sentry')


# Forward reference arg here to avoid circular import
def get_sentry_client(cfg: 'SentryConfig', sentry_tags: Optional[Dict[str, str]]) -> raven.Client:
    client = raven.Client(
        dsn=cfg.dsn,
        environment=cfg.environment,
        include_paths=['obs'],
        release=raven.fetch_package_version('Observer'),
        tags=sentry_tags or {},
        processors=['raven.processors.SanitizePasswordsProcessor', 'obs.sentry.RemoveNoSentryProcessor'])
    return client
```

issue.title: Fix crashes and fails in forward references
issue.body:
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3340
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3419
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3674
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3685
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3799
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3836
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3881
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/867
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2241
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2399
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/1701
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3016
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3054
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2762
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3575
Fixes https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3990

Currently, forward references don't work with anything apart from classes, for example this doesn't work:
```python
x: A
A = NamedTuple('A', [('x', int)])
```
The same situation is with ``TypedDict``s, ``NewType``s, and type aliases. The root problem is that these synthetic types are neither detected in first pass, nor fixed in third pass. In certain cases this can lead to _crashes_ (first six issues above are various crash scenarios). I fix these crashes by applying some additional patches after third pass. Here is the summary of the PR:
* New simple wrapper type ``ForwardRef`` with only one field ``link`` is introduced (with updates to type visitors)
* When an unknown type is found in second pass, the corresponding ``UnboundType`` is wrapped in ``ForwardRef``, it is given a "second chance" in third pass.
* After third pass I record the "suspicious" nodes, where forward references and synthetic types have been encountered and append patches (callbacks) to fix them after third pass. Patches use the new visitor ``TypeReplacer`` (which is the core of this PR).

Here are two problems that I encountered:
* Third pass (both in ``semanal.py`` and in ``typeanal.py``) was more "shallow" than the second one, some visitor methods were literally ``pass``. It was necessary to update these to match the "depth" of the second pass.
* Now third pass has a link to second pass analyzer, ``self.sem``, same as for first pass. It would be nice to refactor the passes since all three share some code/functionality, there is already https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3459 to track this.

NOTE:  self-referential types are still _not_ properly supported, but now we give a reasonable error for this, not a crash, and they still can be used to certain extent, for example:
```python
class MyNamedTuple(NamedTuple):
    parent: 'MyNamedTuple'

def get_parent(nt: MyNamedTuple) -> MyNamedTuple:
    return nt.parent

x: MyNamedTuple
reveal_type(x.parent)
reveal_type(x[0])
```
results in
```
main:2: error: Recursive types not fully supported yet, nested types replaced with "Any"
main:9: error: Revealed type is 'Tuple[Any, fallback=__main__.MyNamedTuple]
main:10: error: Revealed type is 'Tuple[Any, fallback=__main__.MyNamedTuple]
```
Proper support of recursive types would be much harder (mostly due to (de-)serialization that would require something similar to ``type_ref``), there is a separate issue for this https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/731.

@JukkaL sorry it took a bit longer than expected because of CPython sprint last week.
